text: 🇵🇭 Pan de sal — 'bread of salt' — was the most common breakfast bread in 1880s Philippines, sold by street vendors each morning.
🇵🇭 Colonial Philippine towns were built around the plaza complex: church + convent + municipal hall + market — a physical map of Spanish authority.
🇵🇭 In 1880s Philippines, a parish friar could exile a Filipino without trial — no judge, no hearing, just the friar's order.
🇓🇪 Filipino students who studied in Europe (ilustrados) were viewed with suspicion by Spanish authorities — their education was seen as dangerous.
🇵🇭 Pansit — Chinese-origin noodles — were a staple at Filipino town gatherings, always present at receptions and town celebrations.
🇵🇭 'Capitán' in colonial Philippines was an honorary title for wealthy Filipino elites, not a military rank — Tiago was 'Capitán' because of his wealth.
📖 'Noli Me Tangere' is Latin for 'Touch me not' — words Jesus spoke to Mary Magdalene. Rizal chose this title as a warning about the colonial condition.
🇵🇭 In a colonial town like San Diego, a 'bagong dating' (newcomer) would be noticed within hours — gossip spread faster than official news.
🇵🇭 The tiangge (open-air market) was where Filipino social life happened — not just commerce, but gossip, politics, and community bonding.
📖 Rizal published Noli Me Tangere in Berlin, 1887 — he was 26 years old and nearly penniless, borrowing money to print the first 2,000 copies.
